messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: FinTechCo — follow-up: multi-region perf & next tests

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Goal: validate inference performance and stability for your multi-region flows (US & EU initially, APAC optional) and compare Redwood against your current hyperscaler endpoints.
- Primary metrics you care about: p95 latency for 1k-2k token responses, sustained throughput (rps), cold-start behavior, and regional availability / data residency controls.

Redwood differentiators we discussed (how we’ll approach the eval):
- Unified runtime: same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so tests represent production behavior.
- Smart routing + regional pinning: route traffic to nearest region or pinned region when you need strict residency.
- KV/prefix caching and continuous batching: reduces token cost and improves p95 on steady-state workloads.
- Dedicated capacity options with SLA and private VPC deployments (KMS/HSM integrations) for regulated data.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in parallel):
1) Baseline: simple REST generate requests from your test agents in us-east1 and eu-west1 to our hosted endpoints (no caching) — measure p50/p95, error rate.
2) Production-like: enable prefix caching + batching; repeat same traffic profile.
3) Head-to-head: run the same scenarios against AWS SageMaker/GCP Vertex endpoints you nominate (we’ll coordinate), and collect identical metrics.
4) Residency check: validate that data stays in-region for EU traffic using pinned routing + our audit log sample.

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm we have permission to provision short-lived test tokens and spin up test endpoints in us-east1 and eu-west1?
- Please share infra contact who can supply IP ranges or whitelisting steps.
- I’ve attached a one-pager that outlines the high-level comparison vs hyperscalers and a draft benchmark plan (benchmark-plan.xlsx).

If that looks good I’ll schedule the test window for next week and loop in our infra team (Marissa + Sean) to run the head-to-head.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-onepager.pdf, benchmark-plan.xlsx

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear plan and the one-pager. A couple quick clarifications before we sign off on the runs: 

1) Data residency / encryption: during the tests we’ll need to validate that EU requests never leave eu-west1 and that logs/audit trails are retained in-region. Can you confirm support for customer-managed KMS in EU and whether audit logs can be restricted to EU storage?

2) APAC: we’re evaluating some APAC traffic. Does Redwood support private deployments in GCP ap-southeast1 today or would that require a later on-prem/Dedicated engagement?

3) Cost/ops: can you provide a ballpark for Dedicated capacity pricing for a small reserved pool (1-2 GPUs) in each region so we can budget?

If you can answer the above we’ll give the go-ahead and put Priya on infra coordination.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

Alex —

Short answers up front, then a suggested test scope: 

1) Data residency / KMS: yes — we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in our hosted EU regions and for Private deployments. Audit logs can be configured to write to an EU-only bucket (we’ll provide example IAM policies).

2) APAC private deployment: we currently offer hosted endpoints in ap-southeast1 and can run hosted tests there. Private (on-prem/VPC) in APAC is available via our Private offering but typically requires an enterprise engagement; we can scope this in parallel without blocking the initial benchmark.

3) Dedicated pricing: I can share a range — for a small reserved pool (1x A10G-equivalent) expect ballpark $6k–$9k/month depending on commitment and region. We’ll follow up with an exact quote once we know required throughput and SLA.

Suggested test scope (technical contacts):
- Redwood infra lead: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) — will own test orchestration and metric collection.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, throughput (rps), CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost delta vs hyperscaler.
- Regions: us-east1, eu-west1 (required), ap-southeast1 (optional).
- Head-to-head targets: we recommend SageMaker endpoints (mms/real-time) and Vertex AI; we’ll provide identical request scripts and collection hooks.

I’ve dropped the benchmark scripts and a short runbook into the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-benchmark-scripts

If this looks good, Jordan — will you confirm test window (we have availability Tue/Wed next week) and we’ll request short-lived test tokens and collect IP allowlist from FinTechCo.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
